_comment: COUNTRIES — Aaron: 'we should be able to buy or build anywhere we want... maybe we can
limit it to USA, France, Italy, and England'.
A country IS a Region, the sourcing tier that already existed. What earns it a place is
NOT that it has different rents: expansion was measured and a second restaurant came out
0.4% from pure arithmetic, so more places to put a restaurant fixes nothing by itself.
A country has to change what you can DO.
Three axes, each one a decision that did not exist at home:
tastePulls    - your card does not travel. A concept that won at home can be a hard
sell abroad, which is what makes scouting a country worth doing.
localSuppliers- your usual supplier is still available abroad and is now a bad idea,
because it ships in and arrives four days older. Sourcing re-opens.
laborCost     - not a difficulty dial. It decides which concepts are viable, since a
prep-heavy card is a different proposition in an expensive labor market.
Written in American English throughout, per the project's language rule.

countries.name: United States
countries.description: Home. Cheap labor, wide supply, and a crowd that will try anything once.

countries.name: France
countries.description: Dear to staff and unforgiving about food. They will pay for refinement and will not forgive a shortcut.

countries.name: Italy
countries.description: Superb produce on your doorstep and almost no tolerance for anything fancy done badly. Cheap to source, hard to impress.

countries.name: England
countries.description: A late crowd, a drinking crowd, and rents that punish a big room. The bar carries the kitchen here more than anywhere.
